transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lopez (Redwood AE), Ethan Choi (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (Summit Ledger - Procurement), Liam O'Connor (Summit Ledger - InfoSec), Hanna Ruiz (Summit Ledger - Platform), Diego Marquez (Summit Ledger - Legal, briefed)

Summary:
Short procurement/legal intake to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA thresholds, privileged key (KMS/HSM) expectations, and pilot acceptance criteria. Customer wants clarity on private deployment options, 3rd-party audit evidence, and a timeline for procurement approvals.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and DPA specifics (data residency, deletion, retention)
- SLA: uptime SLAs, latency p95 target, error budgets, credits
- KMS integration: bring-your-own-key (BYOK) vs Redwood-managed KMS, HSM requirements
- Pilot scope and success metrics for procurement approval
- Security artifacts (SOC2, pen test reports, cipher list)

Action items (in-call):
- See metadata action_items list above

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya Lopez: All right thanks everyone for joining, um we appreciate the time. Quick roll call and then we'll jump in.
[00:00:10] Priya Nair: Hi this is Priya, yeah thanks, trying to keep this tight because we have internal finance sync at 4.
[00:00:14] Ethan Choi: Hi everyone Ethan from Redwood infra, I'll handle the technical bits, latency/capacity and KMS mapping.
[00:00:20] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, InfoSec. Focus for me is DPA, keys, and audit logs.
[00:00:25] Maya Lopez: Cool. So agenda, we wanna get clarity on legal redlines, SLA thresholds that matter to you, and confirm pilot acceptance criteria so procurement can move.
[00:00:38] Hanna Ruiz: And we wanna understand the private deployment path too — whether VPC peering or on prem, and what KMS modes are supported.
[00:00:45] Maya Lopez: Totally. A couple quick notes: we'll share the onboarding deck and security pack after this call — link in chat: onboarding-deck.link and security-pack.pdf.

[00:01:20] Priya Nair: On the MSA/DPA side, the legal team flagged two sections: one around data residency for EU customers, and another on retention and deletion semantics for model telemetry. Diego is on the call but he's mostly briefed.
[00:01:36] Diego Marquez: Yeah hi, quick note: we need explicit language around deletion upon contract termination and a mechanism to verify deletion, ideally a signed attestation or audit record.
[00:01:50] Jordan Patel: We can provide deletion logs and an export of the audit trail, we also have options for an eDiscovery package if needed.
[00:01:58] Liam O'Connor: Important for us: KMS. We have an HSM-backed KMS requirement for production keys. We need to know if Redwood supports BYOK to an HSM or if keys must live in Redwood-managed KMS.

[00:02:30] Ethan Choi: Short answer: we support both. For Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS via an HSM-backed provider, or we can configure a Redwood-managed HSM with customer-controlled key material via our KMS bridge. Small caveat: if you want full BYOK where keys never leave your HSM, there are networking and latency implications for token encryption operations, we'll show the perf tradeoffs.
[00:03:05] Hanna Ruiz: Can you quantify the latency hit for envelope operations? If we have to call our KMS every request that could be bad.
[00:03:13] Ethan Choi: Right, so we typically use envelope encryption with a short-lived data key cached on the inference nodes, K V cash — um, KV cache — so per-request KMS calls are rare. The most common path is periodic rewraps. So the runtime latency impact to p95 text generation is minimal.
[00:03:37] Priya Nair: That's good to hear. On the DPA redlines, our counsel is likely to ask for 30 day deletion window and proof that logs are purged after that. Is that feasible?
[00:03:48] Maya Lopez: We can definitely model that in the DPA — 30 day retention for transient telemetry is within our standard options. For full content stored by customers we can add a deletion attestation workflow. We'll mark that as an item for legal redline.

[00:04:20] Liam O'Connor: Also need clarity on subprocessor list and whether you have Data Processing Addendum flow for subprocessors — e.g., who hosts the GPUs? Is it a third party cloud?
[00:04:31] Maya Lopez: We maintain a subprocessors list; for Dedicated and Private, customers can pin to specific regions and provider-hosted pools. We'll send the current subprocessors and the hosting footprint in the security-pack.pdf. Note: for Dedicated we use reserved GPU pools managed by Redwood but hosted on cloud infra; for true on-prem we'll hand over the package.

[00:05:02] Hanna Ruiz: Procurement will want pricing guardrails — if we commit to a pilot and then expand, what's the pricing path? Also curious about credits for missed SLAs.
[00:05:13] Maya Lopez: Pricing: pilot pricing is usage-based with a short trial commit. For production we offer tiered pricing for Hosted and committed Reserved Dedicated. SLA credits are standard — 5% credit for single-month breach, escalate to negotiation for repeated breaches. We can plug specific numbers into a term sheet.
[00:05:34] Priya Nair: We need the term sheet to show the breakpoints for cost — nice to have a simple example for 1M tokens/month vs 10M.
[00:05:43] Jordan Patel: We'll prepare a sample term sheet and a cost simulation spreadsheet; Ethan can annotate expected p95 costs under different batching and quantization profiles.

[00:06:20] Ethan Choi: On the technical acceptance criteria for pilot: we typically ask for a 2 week smoke run with 1k concurrent synthetic requests, validate p95 below X ms (we suggested 250 ms in hosted but Dedicated can get lower), no higher than 0.5% error rate, and basic security checklists passed. Is that inline?
[00:06:37] Hanna Ruiz: 250 ms p95 would be amazing but our prod bar is around 200 ms; if Dedicated can hit 200 that helps procurement.
[00:06:45] Ethan Choi: Okay we'll try to target 200 ms p95 in the Dedicated test lane and document the test harness. We'll add that to the action items.

[00:07:10] Priya Nair: For procurement, timeline is important. We're trying to close budget approval by end of June, so we need legal redlines and a pilot plan before then.
[00:07:19] Maya Lopez: Understood. We'll prioritize the MSA redline and DPA options. Quick question for Diego: are you comfortable with us proposing a deletion attestation or do you need a stronger mechanism like third-party deletion verification?
[00:07:32] Diego Marquez: An attestation vouched by Redwood'll probably be fine for initial contract but long term we may want a periodic audit. SOC2 plus attestation is acceptable to give procurement confidence.

[00:08:05] Liam O'Connor: On logging: we need immutable audit logs, ideally shipped to a customer-owned log collector. Is that possible?
[00:08:13] Jordan Patel: Yes, we support pushing audit events to your syslog/Splunk/CloudWatch in near-realtime for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can request log streaming to a customer-owned destination with an add-on.
[00:08:26] Priya Nair: Good. Another procurement question: if we go Dedicated with reserved capacity, what is the minimum commit term?
[00:08:34] Maya Lopez: Standard is 12 months for reserved Dedicated, but we offer 6-month pilots with pro-rated pricing in some cases. We can craft a pilot-specific commit to align with your procurement window.

[00:09:05] Hanna Ruiz: Network constraints: we have strict egress constraints to certain ASNs. We'll share a list. How does that affect deployment?
[00:09:14] Ethan Choi: We'll need the list. For Private we can operate entirely inside your VPC — no public egress. For Dedicated, we isolate traffic and can whitelist your egress endpoints. Some kernel updates require internet access to mirrors; we can arrange an offline patching plan.

[00:09:45] Priya Nair: We're also asking for additional indemnity carveouts around data breach scenarios. Any curiosities on Redwood's standard indemnity posture?
[00:09:55] Maya Lopez: We have standard indemnity language in the MSA. For enterprise we can discuss narrow expansions but Redwood's position aligns with typical SaaS vendors. We should park that for the legal redline session — Diego and our counsel can hash it out.

[00:10:20] Liam O'Connor: A technical deep-dive question — how do you handle KV cache and model state persistence across nodes during autoscaling? We don't want to hit cold-start token costs.
[00:10:32] Ethan Choi: Runtime uses KV cache sharding and sticky routing for sessions; during scale up we replicate hot KV segments. Cold-starts are smoothed by prefix caching and a short-lived warm pool. You won't see excessive token costs unless your session churn is very high. Sorry I said K V cash earlier, transcription idiosyncrasy.

[00:11:05] Hanna Ruiz: For pilot acceptance we'll want a runbook for failover and automatic fallback: if Dedicated is saturated can requests be routed to a lower-tier model?
[00:11:16] Jordan Patel: Yes, our smart routing policy supports cost-tier fallback; canary routing and biggest compatibility checks. We'll include recommended fallback model variants in the README.

[00:11:50] Priya Nair: Back to SLAs: we need to see what the error budget looks like, and whether credits are automatic or require a claim.
[00:11:58] Maya Lopez: Credits are usually claim-based with automated telemetry to help validate. For high tier enterprise we can enable automated credit triggers. We'll include that option in the term sheet.

[00:12:25] Diego Marquez: I just want to flag that we may need an audit clause: an annual third-party security assessment that we can reference. Is Redwood okay with that?
[00:12:35] Maya Lopez: Yes, we publish SOC2 and pen test summaries. For contractual language we can reference annual third-party assessments and provide summaries; full reports are under NDA typically.

[00:13:02] Hanna Ruiz: On the pilot scope, what's the minimum dataset you need from us to run a realistic pilot? Do you need production prompts or can you use synthetic traffic?
[00:13:12] Ethan Choi: Synthetic traffic is fine for perf. For quality/regression tests we prefer a prompt set — redwood-evals-like — that represents your workload. You can share an anonymized prompt set or we can help mask PII.
[00:13:35] Priya Nair: We'll likely provide anonymized prompts. Also, procurement will want an estimate of total cost for a 2-week pilot.
[00:13:43] Maya Lopez: We'll produce a pilot budget estimate, including a Dedicated test lane and staff time for onboarding.

[00:14:10] Liam O'Connor: A security nuance: key rotation frequency — we want to define a rotation window and whether Redwood forces rotations.
[00:14:19] Ethan Choi: Customers can define rotation policies; we enforce via the KMS bridge. We can integrate your KMS rotation schedule and push notifications if keys are rotated unexpectedly.

[00:14:45] Hanna Ruiz: Question from Prod engineering: how do we handle model version pinning across rollouts? We need deterministic behavior for A/B tests.
[00:14:54] Jordan Patel: You can pin model versions per route and roll out via canary policies. Rollbacks are instantaneous to the previous pinned version. We'll share the console demo.

[00:15:20] Priya Nair: Are there any carveouts around export controls for certain model weights or embeddings?
[00:15:29] Maya Lopez: For non-US data residency we can route to EU regions. Export control specifics depend on model licensing; we'll highlight any restricted models in the model catalog.

[00:15:55] Diego Marquez: Legal also wants to know about subcontractor flow for logging providers. Who has access to the logs in Redwood's stack?
[00:16:03] Jordan Patel: Access is role-based. For Dedicated we can map roles and restrict Redwood staff access to privileged operations with just-in-time approvals. We can add a runbook for privileged access.

[00:16:34] Priya Nair: Anything else on pricing approvals that procurement needs? Payment terms? PO flow?
[00:16:41] Maya Lopez: Standard is net 30; for enterprise we support negotiated payment terms. PO flow: procurement sends PO referencing the SOW and we invoice per the term sheet. We'll include a sample PO template.

[00:17:05] Hanna Ruiz: For the pilot, can Redwood provide a quick onboarding checklist for infra folks so platform can pre-provision network and IAM?
[00:17:13] Jordan Patel: Absolutely — we'll include a checklist and a preflight script; it lists required ports, IAM roles, and routing rules.

[00:17:45] Ethan Choi: Returning to performance: we'll put together a short benchmark plan. For Dedicated test lane we'll use a synthetic generator with your latency targets and also try a small sample of anonymized prompts for quality checks.
[00:17:58] Priya Nair: Do you have any reference customers with similar PKI/KMS requirements?
[00:18:05] Maya Lopez: Yes, we can anonymize references, I'll include a short list in the security pack. Some names in finance and health who use BYOK patterns.

[00:18:34] Liam O'Connor: About the DPA; does Redwood accept a 3rd party subprocessor flow where we require notification 30 days before adding new subprocessors?
[00:18:43] Maya Lopez: We can include a 30-day notice clause; some subprocessors are cloud infra and can't be foreseen but we can agree to notify and offer mitigation for material changes.

[00:19:12] Hanna Ruiz: Ok for timeline recap: Priya wants legal redlines done this week — can we do that?
[00:19:20] Maya Lopez: We'll circulate a redline-friendly MSA today and set a redline session next week.

[00:19:50] Priya Nair: I'll confirm procurement window and circulate names for the PO approvers.

[00:20:05] Maya Lopez: Quick note: competitor question — if procurement asks about BigCloudAI offerings, we provide a side-by-side on latency and pricing. ModelServeX does deeper custom on-prem integration but longer lead times.
[00:20:20] Priya Nair: Noted.

[00:20:50] Ethan Choi: Technical aside: if you request full BYOK with zero-key-exit, we can do an HSM proxy architecture but you'll see slight increase in rotation/unwrap latency. We'll quantify in the benchmark.

[00:21:12] Hanna Ruiz: On observability: does Redwood give token-level cost visibility for our teams?
[00:21:20] Jordan Patel: Yes token-level cost breakdown in the Console; we can enable team-level views for billing and set per-route quotas.

[00:21:58] Priya Nair: A question on cancellation: if we terminate early on a reserved Dedicated contract what's the typical refund or exit?
[00:22:06] Maya Lopez: Standard term is pro-rated for remaining commitments but specifics depend on negotiation. For pilots there's usually no termination penalty. We'll surface the term options in the term sheet.

[00:22:40] Diego Marquez: Are there SLA exclusions for force majeure or scheduled maintenance?
[00:22:47] Maya Lopez: Yes exclusions are standard. We'll include a maintenance window definition and emergency maintenance process.

[00:23:10] Hanna Ruiz: For pilot logging, can we get a sample of the audit event schema?
[00:23:17] Jordan Patel: We'll attach a sample audit schema to the security pack and the preflight checklist.

[00:23:50] Priya Nair: Anything blocking us from getting a 6-month pilot signed this month?
[00:23:58] Maya Lopez: Two things: legal redlines and procurement PO timing. If we get redlines this week and procurement confirms budget, we can run the pilot next week.

[00:24:30] Ethan Choi: I'm going to note the performance target: try for 200 ms p95 in Dedicated test lane and run the synthetic 1k concurrent test.

[00:24:45] Priya Nair: We'll aim to give you the prompt set and the network egress list by Monday.

[00:25:00] Maya Lopez: Great — I'll follow up with the MSA redline and term sheet. Jordan will attach the preflight checklist and security pack. Ethan will do the perf plan.

[00:25:30] Hanna Ruiz: Quick doc ask: can you include a sample SLA credit calculation example? Procurement likes the math.
[00:25:38] Jordan Patel: Yes we'll add a credit calc example and a sample invoice.

[00:26:05] Diego Marquez: One more legal nuance: can we get a clause that allows us to do an on-site audit within business hours with reasonable notice?
[00:26:13] Maya Lopez: We'll raise that with Redwood legal; sometimes we provide redacted artifacts under NDA instead of on-site audits, but we'll see.

[00:26:45] Priya Nair: If we do a pilot and expand, do you offer committed volume discounts?
[00:26:53] Maya Lopez: Yes tiered discounts with clear breakpoints; we'll include 3 example breakpoints in the term sheet.

[00:27:20] Ethan Choi: Note: for model rollouts, we can support per-route A/B and pinning. We'll provide a short runbook.

[00:27:40] Hanna Ruiz: Any dependencies on our side we should prep now?
[00:27:46] Jordan Patel: Mainly network allowlists, minimal IAM roles, and sample prompts. The preflight script lists everything.

[00:28:10] Priya Nair: Okay let's summarize and call out owners.
[00:28:16] Maya Lopez: Summary: Maya sends redline MSA and term sheet; Ethan runs perf tests and shares results; Jordan provides security-pack, onboarding checklist, audit schema; Hanna shares network egress and prompts; Priya confirms procurement timeline.

[00:28:40] Priya Nair: That works. Any risks we haven't covered?
[00:28:45] Liam O'Connor: I think the main residual risk is subprocessor changes mid-contract; the 30 day notice helps.
[00:28:52] Maya Lopez: We'll add the subprocessor notice clause as a negotiation point.

[00:29:10] Diego Marquez: One last ask: please include contact for Redwood's security lead in the security pack so legal can follow up.
[00:29:17] Jordan Patel: Will do.

[00:29:40] Maya Lopez: Alright, thank you everyone for the productive session. We'll follow up with the materials and schedule the redline session.
[00:29:50] Priya Nair: Thanks.
[00:30:02] Hanna Ruiz: Thanks all.
[00:30:10] Maya Lopez: End.

Notes on transcription: a few words mistranscribed (e.g., KV cache as K V cash) and occasional speaker mislabels; this is an automated export. Shared artifacts: onboarding-deck.link, security-pack.pdf, pilot-cost-sim.csv (to be uploaded).
